_comment: Positions ledger for report.py. The trading session maintains it: a buy APPENDS, a sell REMOVES. sleeve = swing|momentum (NO 'legacy' — every position is judged each run with a take-profit / trail / hold / thesis-check action; treat the book as an income / grow-the-balance portfolio). Stops are TRAILING: a winner carries a GTC stop ~15% below its running high, ratcheted UP only and never below entry, so it can only ever be sold for a locked-in gain; underwater names carry NO price stop and are thesis-managed (sell only if the thesis breaks, else cull at the monthly rebalance). Options positions (sleeve:'options') may carry a 'manual_hold_override' field to suspend ONLY the mechanical -50% price stop (see CLAUDE.md HARD RULE 8) — settable/clearable only by a genuinely interactive session with a real, live Ryan turn, never by an automated run (same bar as HARD RULE 9).

_monitoring_mandate.posture: MONITOR + RECOMMEND + ASK. Ryan makes the call; the desk's job is to bring him a decision at the right moment with the numbers attached. This CONFIRMS the conservative ask-first default recorded in _open_questions_for_ryan q1 and CLOSES that question: discretionary exits on these two are NOT taken mechanically, they are recommended to Ryan and wait for his go-ahead.
_monitoring_mandate.THE_ONE_EXCEPTION: The unconditional hard premium backstops still EXECUTE without waiting (-65% at 21-45 DTE, -70% above 45 DTE, and the -50% cut once a contract is inside 21 DTE, per the 2026-08-05 exit-method amendment). They exist precisely so a true loser cannot ride toward zero during the hours or days it may take Ryan to see a message and reply. If a backstop executes, notify him immediately AFTER, with the reason. Everything short of a backstop is a recommendation, not an action. Ryan can lift this exception at any time; until he does it stands, because a 15-minute ask-first loop with no floor is how a -50% becomes a -90%.
_monitoring_mandate.HONEST_LIMIT_TELL_HIM_AGAIN_IF_ASKED: This is a 15-minute scheduled cadence during market hours (9:30-16:00 ET), NOT continuous tick-by-tick monitoring. Two real consequences: an intraday spike can round-trip entirely between two runs and never be seen, and an overnight or weekend gap is not covered at all -- the first run of the next session sees the result, not the move. Sizing and expectations must assume gaps between runs. Do not promise Ryan coverage this system does not have.
_monitoring_mandate.SILENCE_RULE_READ_THIS_BEFORE_PUSHING: At ~26 runs/day, an un-deduped mandate turns into 26 notifications a day and Ryan stops reading them -- which destroys the mandate's whole purpose. So: notify ONLY on a trigger below FIRING or UN-FIRING, never on routine state. Each position carries a _notify_state that every run OVERWRITES in place. Before pushing, check last_notified_trigger: if the SAME trigger is still the live one and nothing material has changed, DO NOT notify again -- update the timestamp and mark and stay silent. Re-notify only when a DIFFERENT trigger fires, a fired trigger un-fires, or the recommendation itself changes. A position quietly working is not news; the journal and the EOD report already carry it.
_monitoring_mandate.WHAT_A_RECOMMENDATION_MUST_CONTAIN: Never send a bare 'consider selling'. Every recommendation carries: the trigger that fired and its measured level; current mark, bid/ask and the spread as % of mid (this determines what an exit actually nets and on RBRK it is punishing); P/L in $ and %; DTE and the theta burn per day; the underlying's level versus its written invalidation; the specific alternatives with their trade-offs; and a plain-language RECOMMENDATION with a reason. Ryan asked for this so he can learn how the decision is made -- show the reasoning, not just the verdict.

_LEGGING_TESTED_AND_BLOCKED.the_mechanism: A spread's risk offset exists ONLY INSIDE a multi-leg order. Sent alone, leg two is not 'the short leg of a spread' -- the broker cannot know a long 695P is meant to cover it -- so it is margined STANDALONE as a cash-secured put and demands the entire strike in collateral. Legging destroys the exact property that makes a vertical capital-efficient. A legged CALL spread is worse: a standalone short call is NAKED (cash.infinite=true), banned outright at any level.
_LEGGING_TESTED_AND_BLOCKED.why_this_upgrades_the_prior_warning: CLAUDE.md already warned that a rejected leg two would leave an orphaned full-premium single leg. That was rated a RISK. This measurement makes it a CERTAINTY: leg one fills, leg two is rejected for collateral, and the sleeve owns a position it never decided to own at 4-9x the vertical's theta. Long-first ordering prevents a naked short; it does NOT prevent the orphan.
_LEGGING_TESTED_AND_BLOCKED.review_is_trustworthy_HERE_do_not_overge: The multi-leg FALSE GREEN happens because multi-leg SUPPORT is validated only at the place endpoint. This is a COLLATERAL/buying-power check, which review does perform and did surface correctly. So a clean review still proves nothing about multi-leg support, but a review raising a collateral alert is real and must be honoured.
_LEGGING_TESTED_AND_BLOCKED.the_workflow_that_DOES_preserve_spread_e: Do not leg it, and do not quietly substitute a single leg and call it the same trade. When a thesis genuinely wants a vertical: fully spec it -- both legs, net debit, max profit, breakevens, invalidation -- and hand it to Ryan to place in the Robinhood app, where multi-leg works normally. Desk does the analysis, Ryan does the execution. The permanent fix is agentic multi-leg support.
_LEGGING_TESTED_AND_BLOCKED.nothing_was_placed: This was review_option_order only, which does not place. No order was sent, no position opened, and no naked short was ever created or contemplated -- the review was run precisely to avoid discovering this mid-leg with a live long already on the books.

The discipline paid today, in the only way process discipline ever visibly pays: a loss that did not happen.

Practical consequence for the next run: a QQQ tactical is an increasingly poor expression of what is actually a one-stock flow, and NVDA itself is un-enterable into a print the exit engine says to close before, not open into.

_SPREAD_SOURCING_UNRESTRICTED.authority: Ryan, REAL live turn 2026-08-24 (typed user turn, same message as the band widening): "It can look at any name for spreads."
_SPREAD_SOURCING_UNRESTRICTED.rule: The debit-spread hunt is NO LONGER confined to the core IV list or the equity report's universe. Survey ANY name for a vertical.
_SPREAD_SOURCING_UNRESTRICTED.why_this_is_coherent: Spreads cannot be placed through the agentic API at all (multi-leg refused with HTTP 400; legging refused on collateral -- see _LEGGING_TESTED_AND_BLOCKED). The desk SPECS them and Ryan PLACES them in the app. So the name universe never needed to be limited to what the desk itself can execute.
_SPREAD_SOURCING_UNRESTRICTED.WHAT_DID_NOT_CHANGE: The LIQUIDITY GATE. CORE still requires <=10% of mid and real OI, quoted on the MONTHLY board at the TARGET DELTA. This is a change to WHICH NAMES are eligible, not to WHAT QUALIFIES. Widening the universe without holding the gate would re-create the 2026-08-14 freeze, where four of five candidates died on bid/ask at 12-50% of mid.
_SPREAD_SOURCING_UNRESTRICTED.ordering: Screen liquidity EARLY -- price the vertical BEFORE the thesis workup. A wider universe multiplies the cost of researching untradeable chains, so the 30-second spread check matters MORE now, not less.
_SPREAD_SOURCING_UNRESTRICTED.deliverable_shape: Both legs, net debit, max profit, breakevens, the invalidation level on the underlying, and the intended hold period -- complete enough for Ryan to place without re-deriving anything. NEVER quietly substitute a single leg and call it the same trade.
